Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training

test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.

standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.

shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from recent intent, though it does not establish gains on this exact benchmark. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) combines temporal embeddings with separate long-/short-term attention networks; it reports improvements on sparse Amazon Beauty/Games, while acknowledging weaker performance with limited histories. [HeteroTempRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025525008369) combines local convolutions, global Transformer dependencies, temporal adaptive fusion, and gated historical blocks. These provide architectural precedents for learning when recent behavior should outweigh older interests.

Multi-interest modeling offers another direction. [D2MFRec (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) gates single-interest and multiple-interest representations, then applies denoising contrastive learning; its discussion flags overly dispersed dynamic-routing representations under sparse, irregular behavior. [MIMAR-SRec (2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intent across contextual windows with prototype alignment and robustness training. Practical inference for a lightweight SASRec trial: retain its recent-context representation, add masked historical pooling with a few learned interest queries, and learn a sigmoid fusion gate conditioned on representations, observed history length, and timestamp gaps. Ablate pooling, gating, and multiple interests separately against tuned SASRec. These papers motivate the hypothesis; they do not validate improvement under the specified four-category, sampled-candidate macro HR@10 protocol.

---

Recent work supports testing candidate discrimination before attributing weak rankings to embedding collapse; it does not establish the cause of Electronics performance. [gSASRec (2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) identifies overconfidence from negative sampling and proposes calibrated gBCE, recommending 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75. [Scaled cross-entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14238) finds that loss choice can substantially strengthen traditional sequential recommenders; when full softmax is impractical, scaling the sampled normalization term is an effective alternative.

Harder negatives require care. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports early training failures from introducing hard negatives too soon, motivating uniform warm-up followed by efficient candidate recall and curriculum sampling. [RoDPO (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29259), in multimodal sequential recommendation, reports better ranking with stochastic sampling from dynamic top-K pools than deterministic hardest-negative selection, attributing gains partly to reduced false-negative suppression. Transfer to ID-only SASRec remains unverified.

Compute matters alongside hardness: [CCE− (2025, revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09682) reports up to 2× faster training and over 10× lower memory for sampled CE, with benefits from balancing negative count and batch size. Practical inference: compare multi-negative sampled softmax and calibrated gBCE first; then test a uniform/stochastic-hard mixture after warm-up, excluding observed training positives. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10 at matched GPU time, report Electronics separately, and track throughput and rank changes. Larger training margins alone cannot establish ranking gains or diagnose collapse.

---

Recent work supports learning directional item relationships separately from broad similarity. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) constructs a directed, weighted item graph from interaction histories, combining co-purchase strength with temporal ordering. It offers a lightweight alternative to neural similarity retrieval without pretrained weights. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models both relevance and dissimilarity through low-pass and mid-pass graph filters: complements can be related while differing substantially in function or appearance.

Compatibility remains a separate uncertainty. [ECCR (2024)](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2024/Li.pdf) emphasizes that co-purchase does not establish complementarity, and a plausible product-type pairing does not establish item-level compatibility. Its method fine-tunes an LLM, so it does not meet the scratch-only constraint; its distinction between behavioral association and actual compatibility remains useful. Interaction sequences alone cannot reliably label substitutes versus complements.

For this benchmark, a plausible adaptation—not a published result—is a SASRec residual combining smoothed directed transition scores with separate source/target embeddings and a small title/description encoder trained from scratch. Token or character features could capture explicit model identifiers and compatibility phrases. Keep text similarity and transition evidence as separate signals; treat missing compatibility evidence as unknown. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction histories with item and positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward layers. It predicts the next item by scoring candidate embeddings against the sequence representation. Attention selects relevant past interactions, supporting both recent transitions and longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
